heading: INT. ST. BRIDGET'S CHURCH BASEMENT - NIGHT

units.text: INT. ST. BRIDGET'S CHURCH BASEMENT - NIGHT
Folding chairs in a circle on cracked linoleum.
A coffee urn sputters.
Under a flickering tube light, six people sit with paper cups, and one of them is wearing a wire.

Dana Whitlock, 30s, sharp-eyed, an undercover agent in a thrift-store cardigan, sits beside Walter Pruitt, 60s, a retired accountant who hasn't touched his coffee, while across the circle Rosalind Kerr, 50s, a lawyer with ink-stained fingers, grips the arm of Tomas Reyes, 20s, who bounces his knee, and Father Gil Moran, 70s, the host, folds his hands as Priya Anand, 40s, a nurse in scrubs, steps in late and closes the door too carefully.
CLOSE ON Dana's cup.
A pinhole lens in the rim.
I'm Dana. I'm an alcoholic.
units.name: DANA

units.text: Hi, Dana.
units.name: ALL

units.text: ANGLE ON Walter.
He watches her hands, not her face.
This is the last time any of them will sit in this room together.
You sound new.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: Three weeks.
units.name: DANA

units.text: Funny. You smell like gun oil.
units.name: WALTER

units.text: Silence.
The urn gurgles.
Rosalind's grip on Tomas tightens.
INSERT - Priya's phone, face-down on her knee.
A text lights the screen: HE KNOWS.
WE SEE Father Moran slowly stand, one hand sliding into his cassock.
BACK TO SCENE
Nobody move.
units.name: TOMAS

units.text: Sit down, son. Everyone sit. Dana, the cup, please.
units.name: FATHER MORAN

units.text: Dana sets it on the floor.
Slowly.
